newsitem.title: UK: June overhang keeps North Sea crude under pressure.
newsitem.headline: June overhang keeps North Sea crude under pressure.

text.p: North Sea crudes took another hammering on Tuesday as benchmark Dated Brent extended its recent slide and differentials for other grades crumpled under the weight of unsold June cargoes, traders said.
Brent loading June 17-19 moved between traders at July Brent -70 cents, eight cents weaker than a deal on Monday.
"We're as bearish as hell here. There's still a lot to go in June and the July programmes will be out soon," said a trader.
An overhang of June loading cargoes and a tight transatlantic arbitrage were painting a bleak outlook for North Sea sellers, traders said.
Apart from Brent, Norwegian Oseberg and Statfjord were particularly vulnerable to further losses with a handful of June cargoes still left on the market.
"There's a Statfjord offer at Dated +5 (cents) but we're not even seeing bids at Dated parity," said a North Sea trader.
A 600,000-barrel Oseberg cargo due to load June 22-24 fetched a meagre Dated Brent -5 cents on Tuesday, about seven cents weaker than a deal on Monday.
"The differentials are clearly still under a lot of pressure," said another trader.
July Brent paper was steady, gaining 10 cents to $17.66 a barrel by 1730 GMT as were intermonth spreads but CFDs slipped about 10 cents as the Dated market weakened.
Next week's dates traded at July Brent -50 cents, the week after at July Brent -38 cents.
The sole Brent cargo nominated loading June 25-27, deferred from June 14-16, was kept by the equity holder Shell.
The Mediterranean sour crude market held its bullish tone on Tuesday, after a deal for Russian Urals at Dated Brent -$1.18 on Friday was heard followed by a trade at -$1.17 on Monday.
"A lot has been cleared out, and a lot of refiners were hoping to get Iraqi crude earlier," said a trader.
Some traders weren't expecting first flows of rival Iraqi Kirkuk under the second term of the United Nations oil-for-food deal until July.
Other said buyers were likely to hold off buying June barrels anyway given a 20-cent discount for July liftings.
The price for June Kirkuk is set to be Dated Brent -$2.00, and -$2.20 in July, falling in line with Saudi Arab Light.
West African crudes looked weak with June barrels still unsold. A trader was said to have offloaded some end-June Qua Iboe barrels Monday to a U.S. refiner at a soft Dated +23 cents.
